instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an underhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
2. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips until your torso is almost parallel to the floor.
3. Let the bar hang at arm's length below your shoulders, back flat.
4. Pull the bar toward your lower abdomen by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Lower the bar under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your back flat and core braced to protect your spine.
2. Drive with the elbows and squeeze the shoulder blades at the top.
3. Do not use momentum or jerk the bar with your hips.
4. Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a bar across your shoulders behind your neck.
2. Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back until your torso is near parallel to the floor.
3. Keep your knees slightly bent and core braced.
4. Rotate your torso to one side, driving one end of the bar upward.
5. Return to center, then rotate to the other side.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your spine neutral and avoid rounding your lower back.
2. Rotate from the trunk, not just the arms.
3. Move under control to feel the obliques work.
4. Breathe steadily to keep the core braced.

instructions:
1. Attach a straight bar to a low cable pulley.
2. Stand facing the machine, feet shoulder-width apart, holding the bar with an underhand grip at shoulder width.
3. Keep your elbows tucked close to your sides and arms extended.
4. Curl the bar up toward your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms still.
5. Lower the bar under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and do not lean back.
2. Hold your upper arms still so the biceps do the work.
3. Squeeze the biceps at the top of each rep.
4. Lower slowly to keep tension on the muscle.

instructions:
1. Attach a straight bar to a low cable pulley.
2. Stand facing the machine, feet shoulder-width apart, holding the bar with an underhand grip wider than shoulder width.
3. Keep your elbows tucked close to your sides and arms extended.
4. Curl the bar up toward your shoulders by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms still.
5. Lower the bar under control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your torso upright and do not lean back.
2. The wide grip emphasizes the inner biceps, so keep elbows fixed.
3. Squeeze the biceps at the top of each rep.
4. Lower slowly to keep constant tension.
